title: How to Prepare for System Design Interviews
summary: A practical preparation loop: build the foundation, practice under time pressure, and review your gaps.
keyPoints: Preparation is a loop of study, timed practice, and review, not a reading list.
Pick a path based on your calendar; urgent interviews need the framework and one complete rep.
Build the foundation in order: delivery framework, core concepts, key technologies, then patterns.
Attempt each design before reading the reference, then compare decisions and note gaps.
Track weak patterns across reps and spend extra time on the ones that repeat.
The week of the interview is for light review, two or three mocks, and sleep.

complexity.note: Framework, core concepts, key technologies, patterns.
Attempt first, then read the reference.
Name two gaps and the next action.
Catches vague claims and time management.

commonMistakes: Reading designs and walkthroughs without ever drawing one from a blank page.
Practicing only familiar prompts and avoiding the areas that stay weak.
Spending the week before the interview on new technologies instead of review and mocks.
Scheduling many designs with no time to compare, review, and repeat.
interviewNotes: Rehearse a two-minute opening that states the plan and the assumptions.
Practice with a timer so you learn how much depth fits in the session.
Keep a one-page sheet of numbers, framework steps, and failure questions.
Use each mock to test one weak pattern, not to prove you know everything.

checkYourself.question: Why is reading a reference before an attempt a weak study method?
checkYourself.answer: It creates familiarity with the answer without testing whether you can produce the design from a blank page. Attempt first, then compare decisions.

checkYourself.question: How should an experienced candidate with one week prepare?
checkYourself.answer: Take one diagnostic design, run three timed reps on unfamiliar prompts, and spend the remaining time on the two weakest patterns with a mock.

checkYourself.question: What belongs in a weak-pattern log?
checkYourself.answer: The prompt, the area that broke, and the next action. Repeats across entries show which topic deserves the next practice session.
